question.leadin: Answer some questions about the early colonization of New England.
question.text: This Puritan minister founded Rhode Island after being expelled from Massachusetts. He was one of the first abolitionists and wrote the first book about Native American languages.
question.clue: Earlier in his life, he chafed at Archbishop William Laud's strict control of Anglican Church doctrine, escaping with his wife Mary to Boston.

swap.leadin: This woman took the name Rebecca after converting to Christianity and later married John Rolfe.
swap.text: In a heavily embellished account, John Smith credited what daughter of Chief Powhatan with saving him from an execution?
swap.clue: A governor who issued the statement "He that will not work, shall not eat" prior to the Starving Time may have been saved by this person in a ceremony.

question.leadin: The Battle of Jumonville Glen began this war, after which British colonial forces retreated to Fort Necessity.
question.text: Identify this war, named for the two forces allied against British and colonial troops. This conflict was part of the larger Seven Years' War.
question.clue: Daniel de Beaujeu ("boh-ZHOH") won this war's Battle of Monongahela ("muh-non-guh-HEE-luh"), where General Braddock died trying to reach Fort Duquesne ("dyoo-KAYN").

swap.text: Originally intended as a fort to protect the Dutch West India Company's fur interests in the area, this settlement was handed over to the British in exchange for a tiny island near Suriname in the Treaty of Breda. This settlement was later renamed New York City.
swap.clue: A fort in this settlement was constructed by what became a non-Ohio Bowling Green.

question.text: Mary Beth Norton argued that this event should be understood within the context of King William's War. This 1690s event led to the deaths of twenty people who allegedly worked with the devil.
question.clue: They started after doctor William Griggs provided treatment for certain hysterical fits, and "spectral evidence" during these events was allowed by Cotton Mather.

swap.leadin: The 1689 Boston revolt led to the dissolution of this government.
swap.text: Name this government that was last led by Edmund Andros that included Connecticut and 5 other English colonies.
swap.clue: Its first president later became chief justice of New York, and sentenced Jacob Leisler to death for treason.

question.leadin: John Ingram led this rebellion after its namesake leader's death.
question.text: Name this first major rebellion in the American colonies, which was able to successfully send William Berkeley back to England.
question.clue: This conflict began when the Occaneechees were fired upon by colonists and, in its aftermath, Charles II recalled William Berkeley to England.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about colonial American rebellions.
swap.text: This member of the House of Burgesses began a rebellion by raiding the land of neighboring Doeg Indians. He died of dysentery soon after issuing a "Declaration of the People" criticizing his colony's administration.
swap.clue: This man called an Assembly to stamp out corruption and raise tobacco prices.

question.leadin: This event was quashed after the rebels were spotted by a group of men traveling with William Bull, the state's Lieutenant Governor.
question.text: Identify this rebellion organized by a man known as Jemmy.
question.clue: During this event, participants marched toward Spanish Florida from South Carolina carrying a banner that read "Liberty!"

swap.leadin: Name these founders of early American colonies.
swap.text: His disagreements with John Cotton led him to found Hartford in 1636 and draft the Fundamental Orders of Connecticut three years later.
swap.clue: Thomas Welles and Roger Ludlow drafted a document inspired by this man's theories which was signed by the cities of Wethersfield and Windsor and which guaranteed universal manhood suffrage.

question.text: The Pilgrims had been attempting to reach this colony before the Mayflower was blown northward. The House of Burgesses was the elected body of the government of this colony, which was founded at Jamestown.
question.clue: In this colony, a Doeg raid on Thomas Matthews's farm devastated the Pamunkey and deposed William Berkeley after he refused a militia appointment agreed upon by the House of Burgesses.

swap.text: The governor in Boston at the time had this last name. A woman named Anne with this surname was a religious leader who was expelled by the Puritans and settled in Portsmouth.
swap.clue: A mob led by Ebenezer MacIntosh ransacked a mansion owned by a man with this surname in the aftermath of the Stamp Act.

question.leadin: This politician suspended the New York legislature after it refused to recognize the Quartering Act.
question.text: Identify this British politician whose set of namesake acts spurred the non-importation movement in the colonies.
question.clue: A series of five acts named for this man aimed to enforce the Quartering Act in New York and to save the British East India Company. The placement of British troops in Boston due to those acts eventually led to the Boston Massacre.

swap.text: During the uprising, this group of drunken rangers massacred some unarmed Conestoga Indians in Pennsylvania.
swap.clue: Their first fight was prompted by Matthew Smith's reconnaissance, and Asher Clayton and Lazarus Stewart led their two companies, which were started by Colonel Reverend John Elder.

question.leadin: This explorer followed in the footsteps of the Moor Estevanico, who disappeared in New Mexico in his search for Cibola.
question.text: Name this Spanish explorer who was guided by the Native American "Turk" in his quest to find Cibola, or the Seven Cities of Gold. He was the first European to see the Grand Canyon.
question.clue: After arriving at Quivira and finding mainly rocks and buffalo, this man executed a native guide known as "the Turk."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the English conman Gregor MacGregor.
swap.text: One of MacGregor's few successful forays was taking Amelia Island while expelling the Spanish from this colony. This colony was where the Spanish founded the oldest continuously inhabited settlement by Europeans in North America, St. Augustine.
swap.clue: Forces from this colony lost simultaneous battles at Bloody Marsh and Gully Hole Creek, forcing its parent country to recognize a neighboring colony led by James Oglethorpe.

question.leadin: Name some mythical places sought by Spanish explorers.
question.text: A Zuni referred to as "the Turk" told Coronado of this city in modern day Kansas. Upon reaching this place, Coronado found squash rather than gold.

swap.leadin: Benjamin Franklin created the "Join or Die" cartoon for this meeting.
swap.text: Identify this 1754 meeting convened to discuss treaties between the Iroquois and Mohawk and the American colonies.
swap.clue: Peter Wraxall served as its chronicler, repeatedly referencing the "Fire of Friendship".

question.text: The owner of Onesimus had previously been involved in another controversy when he wrote this 1693 book defending his conduct in the Salem witch trials. This text argues an "army of devils" was attacking "the Puritan colony."
question.clue: This book that includes transcripts of people describing the deeds of Martha Carrier. It includes a prefatory letter by judge William Stoughton, who presided over the events it concerns.

swap.leadin: Among the locations where the provisions of this bill stipulated were acceptable include the taverns of sellers of metheglen, sellers of wine and victualing houses.
swap.text: Name this British act that required colonists to perform the namesake action for soldiers; its unfairness inspired the third amendment of the bill of rights.
